title: campanula rotundifolia subsp. paenina
intro: Campanula rotundifolia subsp. paenina, commonly known as Scottish bluebell or Harebell, is a subspecies of flowering plant in the bellflower family. This plant has been traditionally used for its health benefits, which include its ability to calm the nervous system and reduce anxiety, thanks to its sedative and anti-inflammatory properties. The therapeutic actions of Campanula rotundifolia subsp. paenina include its use as a nervine to calm the mind and body, and as an antispasmodic to relieve muscle spasms. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and saponins, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
